context: Note that (R, S) is of 12 -O elliptic type. Our partial algorithm proves that g has the ultimate sign (+, −, −, +) at 1, i.e., when n ≥ 1, the former sum is greater than and less than the latter sum if n ≡ 0, 3 (mod 4) and if n ≡ 1, 2 (mod 4), respectively. However, for this (R, S), we do not know how to identify the critical lines. Algorithm Hyper [21, Chapter 8] declared that there is no explicit formula like (8) (more precisely, “closed form”). By numerical analysis using our partial algorithm, we find that the slope of the critical line between IR,S (+, −, −, +) and IR,S (+, +, −, −) is in the interval (−2.452, −2.434), and the one between IR,S (+, +, −, −) and IR,S (−, +, +, −) is in (4.8094, 4.816). Theorem 10 can be described in a reduction form: ▶ Theorem 12. For second-order holonomic sequences, the Ultimate Sign Problem Turingreduces to the Minimality Problem.
